race_source.title: Town of Halton Hills — Filed Nominations

nonresponse_source: Chris Golden’s report in this conversation; no complete thread audit or reason for nonresponse established.

races.title: Ward 1 · Four replies, two seats
races.takeaway: Shanna leads all six reviews. There is no unanimous second place.
races.narration: Ward one elects two local councillors. Shanna Maltby’s reply scores highest with all six reviewers. Her advantage is a process: pilots, measurement, safeguards and financial scenarios. The reviewers disagree on second place among Galati, Carruthers and Albano. Their answers offer different strengths: sharing productivity gains, warning about displacement, and adopting tools where they add public value. This measures the replies, not a predicted election result.

races.title: Regional · Wards 1 and 2
races.takeaway: Alex leads all six reviews. Both replies need a funding mechanism.
races.narration: For regional councillor in wards one and two, Alex Hilson’s reply scores higher than Hillary Spurr’s with every reviewer. Hilson provides more concrete examples and evidence of engagement. Spurr puts essential workers, trades and human judgment at the centre. Neither reply sets out a detailed funding response if employment pressure arrives before savings. This is one regional race, not all regional candidates.

races.title: Mayoral · One supplied reply
races.takeaway: Jason is the only mayoral respondent in this exercise.

Ann Lawlor and Ivan Bosnjak did not answer, as reported by the organiser, so they receive no grade. Jason takes the participation result by default in this exercise. That gives us a reply to assess; it cannot establish that his answer would outperform answers we never received.

future_gap.headline: A transition plan for faster change.
future_gap.narration: The biggest shared future gap is the transition itself. Several replies acknowledge jobs, risk and uncertainty, so this is not a claim that they ignored disruption. But much of the response stays at the level of useful tools, efficiency, skills or historical reassurance. What is mostly missing is a timed plan connecting changing work, household pressure, service demand and public finances, including the period before promised savings or new opportunities arrive.
future_gap.display:
Changing work can pressure households and businesses
Service demand and public finances may shift
Savings and new opportunities may arrive later
The missing bridge: a funded, timed transition plan.

scenarios.title: Gradual adoption
scenarios.body: Measure useful gains. Train staff. Keep alternatives available.

scenarios.title: Rapid disruption
scenarios.body: Track local work and household pressure. Coordinate support and funding.

scenarios.title: Savings disappoint
scenarios.body: Protect priority services. Set spending limits and a fallback.

future_gap.scenario_narration: The advice is to prepare for more than one pace of change. For gradual adoption, measure real gains and build skills. For rapid disruption, track local pressure and coordinate a response with the governments responsible. If promised savings disappoint, protect priority services and use a funded fallback. These are planning scenarios, not forecasts or claims that job losses are inevitable.

candidate_advice.title: Turn the process into a funded first step.
candidate_advice.advice: Name the first pilot, its owner, cost and deadline. Add a service-funding fallback if savings are small.
candidate_advice.narration: For Shanna, the main opportunity is to make the process executable: name the first pilot, its owner, cost and deadline. Add a service-funding fallback if savings are small.
candidate_advice.basis: Pilot measurement and safeguards are already present; operational and fiscal detail would strengthen them.
